title: Happy Number
keyIdea: Repeatedly replace n by the sum of the squares of its digits. The sequence either reaches 1 (happy) or falls into a cycle. Detect the cycle with Floyd's slow/fast pointers instead of a set: slow takes one step, fast two; if they meet somewhere other than 1, it loops forever.

approaches.name: Floyd, do-while
approaches.idea: Your commented version: do { slow 1 step, fast 2 steps; if slow == 1 return true } while (slow != fast); return false.
approaches.why: Numbers drop below 243 almost at once, and the cycle there is short; two ints of state.

approaches.name: Floyd, while loop
approaches.idea: Your active code: loop while slow or fast isn't 1; move them; if they meet at something other than 1, return false. When both are 1, return true.
approaches.why: Same steps as the do-while; two ints of state.

quiz.q: Why must the sequence either reach 1 or repeat?
options: For any number with 4+ digits the digit-square sum is smaller, so values stay in a small range and must repeat

quiz.q: Why does your do-while version need do-while?
options: slow and fast both start at n, so while (slow != fast) would never run

quiz.q: What does slow == fast mean in your while version, when it isn't 1?
options: The numbers are going round a cycle without 1, so n is not happy

steps: Brute force: store every value in a set until 1 or a repeat. Cost?
